messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE — SLO alert: streaming /v1/stream in us-west-2 showing p95=320ms, p99=6400ms over last 5m. Spike started at ~4287659950. Potential streaming stalls + backend tail. Affected model: gpt-3.5-serve-v2 (quant). Dashboard: https://console.redwood.dev/ops/streams?range=15m

jordan: oncall here, taking. tagging eng-runtime + infra. any quick wins to reduce customer impact?

sam: looking at runtime traces — lots of requests stuck in "sending chunks" state. stack shows repeated GPU local queue stalls and long memcpy waits. early sign: ECC correctable errors rising on a host.

bryce: infra telemetry for node gpu-node-47: GPU temps oscillating 78C -> 86C, fan duty flapping, power cap dropping, scheduler reports "freq_throttle" events. ECC correctable count on GPU0 went from 120 to 560 in last 10m. suspect hardware-level degradation causing stalls.

tara: propose immediate mitigation plan: 1) cordon + drain gpu-node-47 to stop new allocations, 2) route streaming traffic away from that rack / AZ, 3) fallback small model for a slice of traffic, 4) reduce batch size and lower max concurrency on stream endpoints. we should do this in steps to avoid churn.

jordan: executing cordon/drain now. command:```bash
kubectl cordon gpu-node-47
kubectl drain gpu-node-47 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force --grace-period=60\```

jordan: drain output: "evicting pods... 12 pods evicted, 3 streaming pods still terminating (in-flight clients)." Those streaming pods hold long-lived connections. we need to avoid abruptly killing streams.

sam: for streaming pods we can stop sending new sessions to instances and set a short keepalive for existing ones; also set model fallback for new sessions. I'll flip routing to prefer dedicated-cold pool.

bryce: toggling AZ routing to avoid the rack where gpu-node-47 lives. doing a soft failover now.

deploy-bot: Automatic action: traffic split updated — 90% -> primary pool, 10% -> fallback (gpt-3.5-lite) for streaming in us-west-2.

lee: support notes — customer impact: monitoring shows 18 customer sessions with >10s stalls; 4 enterprise customers affected. drafting proactive message to customers.

sam: dumping quick diagnostics — nvidia-smi sample:```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 525.78       Driver Version: 525.78       CUDA Version: 12.1  |
| GPU  Name        Temp  Fan  Perf Pwr:Usage/Cap ECC_Correctable 
| 0   A100-SXM4    83C   85%   P2   290W  560  
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

bryce: also checking dmesg: I see repeated messages "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): GPU has fallen off the bus" and "correctable ECC error" entries. hardware team should replace the card; scheduling hot-swap.

tara: scheduling replacement is fine but need live mitigations first. Jordan, can we reduce streaming concurrency and enforce a 30s idle timeout to recover tail?

jordan: lowering concurrency to 1 for streaming route and setting idle timeout to 30s. applying policy patch:```json
{"route": "/v1/stream", "max_concurrency": 1, "idle_timeout_ms": 30000}
```

jordan: policy applied. early telemetry (1m): p99 dropped from 6400ms -> 2100ms but p95 slipped a bit due to lower batching. overall acceptable while we hot-swap.

bryce: hardware ETA update — replacement kit available in 45 min, on-site tech inbound. plan: cordon node now, replace GPU, then bring back after burn-in tests.

lee: sent customer message for affected enterprise customers (standard template). will post status page update and 30-min cadence.

customer-success: we'll follow up with targeted emails after final remediation and offer credits for impacted usage.

tara: post-mitigation checklist: 1) confirm ECC counters reset after swap, 2) monitor p99 for 2 hours, 3) run a synthetic streaming load to verify no stalls, 4) add extra thermal margin on that rack.

sam: logging note — capturing KV cache stats and per-request trace ids for all >2s streaming responses so we can do root-cause correlation offline. dumping trace ids to S3: s3://redwood-incidents/4287659999/traces.json

incident-bot: Incident ticket INC-2026-4287659999 created and assigned to "oncall-sre". priority: P1. next update expected in 30m.

jordan: quick summary: cause suspected hardware degradation on gpu-node-47 (ECC/thermal -> throttle -> streaming stalls). Live mitigations: cordoned node, traffic split to fallback, concurrency lowered, idle timeout enforced. Hardware replacement scheduled (ETA 45m). Customer comms active. handing to infra for swap and to sam for follow-up analysis. leaving oncall.

tara: thanks team. please annotate the incident with decisions and timelines. I'll own the RCA once resolved. :thumbsup:

bryce: will report back when replacement complete and I have ECC counters cleared.

end of thread.
